stem.en: Kabir has a strand GGGGAAAACCCC. He says it cannot fold, "because the G's and the C's are at opposite ends". What happens when he bends it?

text.en: It folds into a hairpin. Bent back, the GGGG end lies against the CCCC end running the other way, G pairs with C four times, and the AAAA becomes the loop.

feedback.en: Far apart along the strand is exactly what folding brings together. The ends meet.

text.en: The A's pair with each other.

feedback.en: A pairs with U only. Four A's in a row have no partner, so they form the loop.

text.en: It folds into a straight line.

feedback.en: A straight strand has no pairs. The hairpin pairs four, which is why it forms.

explanation.en: Look for a stretch and its reverse partner. GGGG and CCCC read against each other in reverse are four G-C pairs. Whatever lies between is the loop.
